purpose: Definitions for the DEV-* endpoint checks emitted by Device/Invoke-TPDeviceCompliance.ps1. The endpoint script owns the check LOGIC (it has to, to run standalone on a bare machine); this file owns the judgement — title, severity, NIST citation, remediation and business risk. Keeping them apart means the endpoint script stays small and dumb and the reporting stays central.
note: These are deliberately NOT in controls.json. That file is the 195 tenant controls, a stated product number; DEV-* controls only produce findings when device results are supplied via -DeviceResults, and mixing them in would silently change the tenant control count. Findings are emitted with Category 'Endpoint' — the vocabulary Add-TPFinding already enforces. The Group field here is finer-grained grouping for this file and the device documents, not a finding category. Nist171 lists the 800-171 Rev 2 requirements each check evidences, used by the SSP generator. Plain requirement IDs rather than CMMC practice IDs on purpose: a CMMC ID encodes a Level, and asserting the wrong Level is a visible error in front of an assessor. Empty means the mapping was arguable and was deliberately left out — an inflated mapping is worse than an honest gap.

controls.Title: BitLocker Protection Enabled on OS Volume
controls.Remediation: Deploy an Intune disk-encryption policy enforcing BitLocker with TPM (plus PIN where the threat model warrants it) and escrow the recovery key to Entra ID.
controls.BusinessRisk: An unencrypted laptop that leaves the building is a reportable data breach rather than a hardware loss. This is the single control that most often decides whether a lost device requires notification.

controls.Title: Fixed Data Volumes Encrypted
controls.Remediation: Extend the BitLocker policy to fixed data drives, not just the OS volume.
controls.BusinessRisk: A second internal drive holding the actual working data is a common blind spot — the OS volume is encrypted and the data is not.

controls.Title: BitLocker Recovery Password Protector Present
controls.Remediation: Ensure the encryption policy creates a recovery password protector and escrows it. Verify the key is visible in Entra ID for the device.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without a recovery protector a forgotten PIN or a TPM change turns an encrypted disk into permanently unrecoverable data.

controls.Title: TPM Present, Enabled and Ready
controls.Remediation: Enable the TPM in firmware and initialize it. Devices without a usable TPM cannot bind BitLocker or Windows Hello to hardware and should be scheduled for replacement.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without a hardware root of trust, BitLocker degrades to a password and Windows Hello cannot bind a credential to the device.

controls.Title: Secure Boot Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable UEFI Secure Boot in firmware. A device installed in legacy BIOS mode needs conversion (MBR2GPT) or a rebuild.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without Secure Boot a bootkit can load before the operating system and before any security product on it.

controls.Title: Virtualization-Based Security Running
controls.Remediation: Enable memory integrity (HVCI) and Credential Guard via an Intune Endpoint Security policy on hardware that supports it.
controls.BusinessRisk: VBS is what isolates derived credentials from a kernel-level compromise; without it a single privileged intrusion yields reusable domain credentials.

controls.Title: Defender Real-Time Protection Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable real-time protection via an Intune antivirus policy. If a third-party AV is primary, confirm its health in that product's console and record it as the compensating control.
controls.BusinessRisk: Real-time protection off means malware is only found on a scheduled scan, which on a workstation may be days after execution.

controls.Title: Defender Tamper Protection Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable tamper protection tenant-wide in the Defender portal, or via an Intune Endpoint Security antivirus policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without tamper protection, any process with administrative rights can simply switch the antivirus off — which is exactly what ransomware does first.

controls.Title: Antivirus Definitions Current
controls.Remediation: Investigate update connectivity for the device. Persistent staleness usually means a proxy, a metered connection, or a device that has not been online.
controls.BusinessRisk: Stale definitions miss the current campaign. A device weeks behind is protected against last month's threats only.

controls.Title: Cloud-Delivered Protection Enabled
controls.Remediation: Set MAPS reporting to Advanced via Intune antivirus policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: Cloud-delivered protection is what catches never-before-seen samples; without it detection falls back to local signatures alone.

controls.Title: Potentially Unwanted Application Protection in Block Mode
controls.Remediation: Set PUA protection to Enabled (block) rather than Audit.
controls.BusinessRisk: PUA covers the adware, bundleware and remote-access tooling that precedes many hands-on-keyboard intrusions.

controls.Title: Attack Surface Reduction Rules Enforcing
controls.Remediation: Deploy the office-macro, script and credential-theft ASR rule set in Block mode. Audit mode first if line-of-business software is unknown, but Audit is not the destination.
controls.BusinessRisk: ASR blocks the specific techniques that start most endpoint intrusions without needing to identify the malware itself. Rules left in Audit report the technique and allow it.

controls.Title: Controlled Folder Access Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable controlled folder access via Intune, with a tested allow-list for line-of-business applications.
controls.BusinessRisk: This is the ransomware-specific control: it stops untrusted processes writing to user document folders even if execution was not prevented.

controls.Title: Defender for Endpoint Onboarded
controls.Remediation: Onboard the device via the Intune Defender for Endpoint connector.
controls.BusinessRisk: EDR telemetry is usually the only way to reconstruct what an intruder did. A device that is not onboarded is invisible after the fact.

controls.Title: Host Firewall Enabled on All Profiles
controls.Remediation: Deploy an Intune firewall policy enabling all three profiles.
controls.BusinessRisk: The host firewall is the control that still applies when the laptop is on a hotel or home network with no perimeter in front of it.

controls.Title: Firewall Default Inbound Action Is Block
controls.Remediation: Set the default inbound action to Block on all profiles; add explicit allow rules for what is genuinely needed.
controls.BusinessRisk: A default-allow inbound profile exposes every listening service on the machine to whatever network it joins.

controls.Title: SMBv1 Not Enabled
controls.Remediation: Remove the SMB1Protocol optional feature and confirm the server-side registry value is not forcing it on.
controls.BusinessRisk: SMBv1 is the protocol WannaCry and NotPetya spread over. It has no safe configuration and no remaining legitimate use in a modern estate.

controls.Title: LLMNR Disabled
controls.Remediation: Set the Turn off multicast name resolution policy (EnableMulticast = 0) via Intune or Group Policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: LLMNR and NBT-NS poisoning is the standard opening move for internal credential capture. It requires no exploit, only a foothold on the same subnet.

controls.Title: RDP Requires Network Level Authentication
controls.Remediation: Where RDP must be enabled, require Network Level Authentication and restrict access by firewall rule and Conditional Access.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without NLA the logon screen is reachable before authentication, which is both a brute-force target and a pre-auth exploit surface.

controls.Title: Local Administrators Group Reviewed
controls.Remediation: Review the membership against who should hold local administrator rights. Remove day-to-day user accounts and use an approved elevation path instead.
controls.BusinessRisk: Most endpoint malware needs administrative rights to persist. Standing admin on a daily-driver account removes that obstacle entirely.

controls.Title: Built-in Administrator Account Disabled
controls.Remediation: Disable the RID 500 account. Renaming it is not sufficient — the SID is what an attacker enumerates.
controls.BusinessRisk: The built-in administrator is the one account guaranteed to exist on every Windows machine, which makes it the default target for password spraying.

controls.Title: Guest Account Disabled
controls.Remediation: Disable the RID 501 guest account.
controls.BusinessRisk: An enabled guest account allows unauthenticated enumeration and, in some share configurations, unauthenticated read access.

controls.Title: LAPS Managing the Local Administrator Password
controls.Remediation: Deploy Windows LAPS via Intune with escrow to Entra ID and automatic rotation. Remove any pre-existing shared local account.
controls.BusinessRisk: A shared local administrator password means one recovered credential unlocks every device that shares it. This is the single most common way a one-machine compromise becomes an estate-wide one.

controls.Title: No Enabled Local Account With Non-Expiring Password
controls.Remediation: Remove PasswordNeverExpires from enabled local accounts, or document the LAPS-managed account as the deliberate exception.
controls.BusinessRisk: A non-expiring local password is a credential that survives every rotation policy the organization thinks it has.

controls.Title: Operating System Build Recorded
controls.Remediation: No action — inventory. Compare the reported build against the servicing branches still receiving security updates.
controls.BusinessRisk: An out-of-support build stops receiving security fixes entirely, which no other control on this list compensates for.

controls.Title: Operating System Updated Recently
controls.Remediation: Deploy Intune update rings with an enforced deadline, and a compliance policy setting a minimum OS version so an unpatched device loses access.
controls.BusinessRisk: Nearly all exploited endpoint vulnerabilities have a patch available at the time of exploitation. The gap between release and installation is the actual exposure.

controls.Title: No Pending Reboot
controls.Remediation: Enforce a reboot deadline in the update ring. A machine that never reboots never finishes patching.
controls.BusinessRisk: A patch installed but not rebooted into is not yet protecting the machine, while the reporting shows it as installed.

controls.Title: Machine Inactivity Lock Configured
controls.Remediation: Set the interactive logon machine inactivity limit via Intune (900 seconds or less is typical for workstations).
controls.BusinessRisk: The unattended desk is the most common physical exposure in any office, and the only one that happens every day.

controls.Title: Screen Saver Requires Re-Authentication
controls.Remediation: Where a screen-saver policy is used, require a password on resume. The machine inactivity limit (DEV-6.1) is the stronger control.
controls.BusinessRisk: A screen saver that does not lock is decoration, not a control.

controls.Title: PowerShell 2.0 Engine Removed
controls.Remediation: Remove the MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root optional feature.
controls.BusinessRisk: The v2 engine bypasses script block logging, AMSI and constrained language mode. Downgrading to it is a standard evasion step.

controls.Title: PowerShell Script Block Logging Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable script block logging via Intune or Group Policy, and confirm the events reach wherever logs are retained.
controls.BusinessRisk: Script block logging is usually the only record of what a fileless PowerShell intrusion actually did.

controls.Title: AutoRun Disabled on All Drive Types
controls.Remediation: Set NoDriveTypeAutoRun to 255 via policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: AutoRun executes attacker-supplied content on insertion, which is what makes a dropped USB stick a working delivery mechanism.

controls.Title: Credential Delegation Protection Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable Restricted Admin mode / protected credential delegation via policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: Limits credentials being left in memory on the machine an administrator connects TO, which is how one compromised server harvests admin credentials.

controls.Title: Process Creation Auditing Includes Command Line
controls.Remediation: Enable Include command line in process creation events via policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: Without it, process-creation events record the binary but not its arguments — and the arguments are where the intent is.

controls.Title: Process Creation Auditing Enabled
controls.Remediation: Enable Audit Process Creation (Success) in the advanced audit policy.
controls.BusinessRisk: Process creation events are the backbone of endpoint investigation. Without them there is no timeline to reconstruct.

controls.Title: Event Log Sizes Meet Minimums
controls.Remediation: Raise the maximum event log sizes by policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Event Log Service): Security to at least 196,608 KB and Application, Setup and System to at least 32,768 KB, or to whatever holds the window your log collection needs.
controls.BusinessRisk: A log that is too small rolls over before anyone collects it, and the oldest events, usually the start of an intrusion, are the first ones lost.

controls.Title: Event Logs Keep Recording When Full
controls.Remediation: Set 'Control Event Log behavior when the log file reaches its maximum size' to Disabled for the Application, Security, Setup and System logs, so a full log overwrites its oldest events instead of stopping.
controls.BusinessRisk: A log set to stop when full can be switched off by anyone who fills it, which is a known way to blind an investigation.

controls.Title: Audit Policy Subcategory Settings Take Precedence
controls.Remediation: Set 'Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings (Windows Vista or later) to override audit policy category settings' to Enabled, or remove the value that sets it to 0.
controls.BusinessRisk: With it off, a category-level audit setting from Group Policy can silently replace the subcategory settings the other audit checks rely on, such as Process Creation.

controls.Title: Sysmon Presence Recorded
controls.Remediation: No action required by this check. It records whether Sysmon is installed. If the endpoint telemetry it provides (process hashes, network connections, image loads) is not collected some other way, such as by the EDR agent, consider deploying Sysmon with a tuned configuration.
controls.BusinessRisk: Native Windows auditing does not record process hashes, network connections or image loads; without Sysmon or an EDR that collects them, an investigation has less to work with.
